title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics, schema mapping, and tool message formatting
author: Maya Patel
description: This PR aligns Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer with the latest function/tool-calling semantics: (1) implement tool_choice resolution semantics to match OpenAI's behavior when multiple tools are available, including deterministic tie-breaking and preferred-tool hints; (2) add schema mapping utilities that translate tool-defined JSON schemas into Redwood validation checks and best-effort coercion rules to support structured outputs; (3) standardize tool message formatting so tool responses are emitted as messages with role="tool" and include a consistent metadata envelope for downstream consumers and telemetry. Motivation: customers using OpenAI-compatible tooling expect predictable tool selection behavior and schema-driven validation for structured outputs. This PR reduces integration friction, fixes several edge cases seen in real customer workloads, and adds comprehensive tests and docs. Changes include implementation, tests, and docs. Checklist: [x] implement tool_choice priority resolver with preferences and deterministic fallback, [x] schema mapper and validator with clear error payloads, [x] message formatter for tool responses and backwards-compatible HTML/plaintext fallbacks, [x] unit and integration tests, [x] docs and example snippets for SDKs, [x] CI and e2e stability verification. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged unless a consumer opts into strict OpenAI-compatible mode via the openai_compat.enable_tool_choice flag. See linked linear tickets ENG-8421 and ENG-8560 for acceptance criteria and rollout plan.
commits: feat(openai-compat): add tool_choice resolver and deterministic fallback logic
feat(openai-compat): implement schema mapper and runtime validator for tool outputs
feat(openai-compat): add message_formatter to emit role="tool" envelope and metadata
test(openai-compat): add unit and integration tests for tool_choice and schema mapping
docs(openai-compat): document tool calling semantics and SDK examples
chore(ci): add compat-ci workflow job and increase e2e timeout for streaming tests
review_comments: Liam Chen: Please clarify deterministic tie-breaking rules when two tools have equal score. Are we using lexicographic order or insertion order?

Maya Patel (author): We use deterministic composite key: (preference flag, provided score, tool registration timestamp, tool name lexicographic) so teams can influence selection via preference flag. Added comment and unit test to demonstrate behavior.
Aria Gomez: The schema mapper currently coerces string->number silently in some cases. We should either make coercion opt-in or surface warnings to the user so silent data loss doesn't occur.
Maya Patel (author): Changed mapper to return a validation result with reasons; coercion is now opt-in via schemaMapping.coerce=true. Updated docs and tests to cover both modes.
Noah Singh: Can we keep backward-compatible tool message shape for clients expecting plain text? What is the migration path?

Maya Patel (author): message_formatter defaults to legacy plain-text payload under metadata. Consumers can opt into full envelope by setting openai_compat.strict_tool_messages=true. Added migration note to docs and an SDK snippet showing how to opt-in.
Liam Chen: CI flake observed in streaming stability tests — increased timeout and made test retry idempotent. Approving after green CI.
Aria Gomez: A couple of minor nits in docs (grammar) — fixed.
release_notes: OpenAI-compat: tool_choice semantics implemented with deterministic fallback; schema mapping and runtime validation for tool outputs; tool message formatting standardized. Opt-in flags: openai_compat.enable_tool_choice, openai_compat.strict_tool_messages, schemaMapping.coerce. See docs/openai-compat/tool-calling.md for migration steps.
